Short answer: I don't see the old JIT/planner flag marked as removed — JIT-related GUCs are still documented and (in the PostgreSQL 19 notes) JIT was made off by default rather than the flag being ripped out. ([postgresql.org](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/jit-configuration.html?utm_source=openai))

A bit of context/precision:
- If by "shipping now" you mean the current stable branch (PostgreSQL 18.x), the recent 18.x release notes and docs still show JIT fixes and the JIT configuration parameters — I didn't find a note saying the old planner flag was removed. ([postgresql.org](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/18.6/?utm_source=openai))  
- If you mean the upcoming/current major (PostgreSQL 19, which has beta releases out), the 19 docs and release notes likewise document JIT configuration and mention that JIT is now off by default — again, not that the old flag was entirely removed. ([postgresql.org](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/19/release-19.html?utm_source=openai))

If you have the exact flag name you mean (for example "jit", "jit_above_cost", or a different historical name), tell me and I’ll double-check the specific deprecation/removal wording in the release notes and config docs.
